# AI Coding Platforms Compared (Individual / Small-Team Lens, April 2026)

**Last revised:** 2026-04-26

## TL;DR

For an individual or small-team buyer in April 2026, **Claude Code on Pro $20/mo is the strongest balance of model quality (Opus 4.7 leads SWE-bench Verified at 87.6% [32]) and surface flexibility (CLI + VS Code + JetBrains + Desktop + Web + iOS [2])**. **Cursor on Pro $20/mo** is the strongest fork-IDE alternative, with Composer 2 as Cursor's own model at $0.50/M input tokens [8]. **GitHub Copilot Pro $10/mo** has the broadest IDE coverage but **cannot be signed up for new today** [12][13]. **Antigravity (free preview)** is currently the cheapest path to Claude Opus 4.6 specifically [19]. **IBM Bob** is genuinely accessible to individuals at $20/mo + $3 support [26][29] but is built around RPG/COBOL/IBM i. **Windsurf Pro $20/mo** with Devin Cloud sessions on Max [22] is the agent-orchestration play.

The four platform events that shaped this comparison fired in the **11 days before this writing**: Windsurf 2.0 + Devin (April 15) [22], GitHub Copilot signup pause (April 20) [13], Anthropic's silent Claude Code pricing flip-flop (April 22) [5], GitHub Copilot training-data policy effective (April 24) [14]. Anything written before mid-April 2026 is dated.

## Decision framework

1. **What's your editor?**
   - **Terminal:** Claude Code Pro ($20) is canonical [1][2]. Gemini CLI (free) is open-source backup.
   - **VS Code (and you'll switch IDEs):** Cursor Pro ($20) [7] or Antigravity preview (free) [18][19].
   - **VS Code (and you won't switch):** GitHub Copilot Pro is ideal but can't be newly subscribed today [12][13]; Claude Code's VS Code extension [2] is the working alternative.
   - **JetBrains / Visual Studio:** GitHub Copilot is the only first-party option [15] — but new Pro signups paused [12]. Claude Code has a JetBrains beta [2].
   - **RPG / COBOL / IBM i:** IBM Bob is purpose-built [26][28].

2. **What's your monthly budget?**
   - **$0:** Gemini Code Assist Individual free (1,000/day) [17] or Antigravity preview free [19] — accept training-data tradeoffs.
   - **~$20/mo:** Claude Code Pro [1] or Cursor Pro [7] or Windsurf Pro [21] or IBM Bob Pro [26] all live here.
   - **~$40-60/mo:** Cursor Pro+ ($60) [7] or GitHub Copilot Pro+ ($39, signup paused) [12].
   - **$100-200/mo:** Claude Code Max [1], Cursor Ultra [7], Windsurf Max with Devin [21], IBM Bob Ultra [26].
   - **Multi-platform stack:** 70% of Pragmatic Engineer 2026 survey respondents juggle 2-4 tools [37].

3. **How much do you care about model freedom?**
   - **Want to swap providers freely:** Cursor [7], Windsurf [24], or Antigravity [18] — all expose Claude/GPT/Gemini directly.
   - **Want one provider's model exclusively:** Claude Code (Anthropic) [2], Gemini Code Assist + CLI (Google) [17], IBM Bob (auto-routed multi-vendor — but you don't pick).

4. **How much do you trust agents to act autonomously?**
   - **High autonomy:** Antigravity Manager Surface [18] or Windsurf 2.0 + Devin [22] for orchestrated multi-agent. GitHub Copilot Coding Agent (cloud, issue-to-PR) [research] is the strongest cloud-only.
   - **Plan-and-review:** Bob's Ask/Plan/Code/Advanced/Orchestrator gradient [26][29] is the most-structured.
   - **Trust regression risk:** Cursor 2.1.50 had silent file emptying bugs in December 2025 [11]; Gemini 2.5 Pro spiraled into 693 lines on a 2-line bug in February 2026 testing [36].

5. **How private do you want to be on the individual tier?**
   - **Maximum privacy:** Cursor Privacy Mode [9] (true ZDR with model providers when enabled), or move up to Business / Enterprise tier on whichever platform.
   - **Default privacy:** GitHub Copilot Free/Pro/Pro+ now uses interaction data for training by default since April 24, 2026 [14]; Gemini Code Assist Individual collects code/prompts for training with opt-out [20]; Anthropic's August 2025 consumer terms presents the choice to users [3]. Across all three, opting out is manual, and the Business / Enterprise / API tiers are excluded from training entirely.
   - **Data residency:** IBM Bob supports customer-cloud deployment [research].

## Honesty section — the productivity claims are mixed

GitHub's controlled study claims Copilot makes developers 55% faster (n=95, controlled task) [16]. METR's RCT measured experienced developers as **19% slower** with AI tools (n=16, real open-source tasks) — and developers perceived themselves as 20% faster anyway [34]. GitClear's analysis of 211M lines of code shows code duplication rising from 8.3% to 12.3% and refactoring rates falling from 25% to under 10% [35]. The Pragmatic Engineer 2026 survey shows enthusiastic adoption with Claude Code as the #1 tool [37]; that's enthusiasm, not measured outcomes. None of this should determine the buying decision, but it should set realistic expectations.
